44.result:
I checked the code: Extract log's success notification already names the destination note and section. So the request is already partly met. I can't write firm requirements until the owner says what's missing (Q1 below).

## What the code does now (answers the owner's reply)

- **Success notice.** After the target note is written and the source is updated, it shows `Extract log: moved child block to "<target basename>" > <section text>` for 4 seconds (`src/commands/extractLog.ts:168-171`, `src/config.ts:15`).
  - The note is shown by its file name only (no folder or `.md`), in quotes.
  - The section is the configured log heading (default `## Log`) with the `#`s removed, so you see `Log` (`extractLog.ts:116`, `src/utils/tasks.ts:20-31`).
- **What the notice leaves out:**
  - The new dated sub-heading the content actually goes under, e.g. `### [[2026-11-09 Mon]] Checkin mit Chris` (`extractLog.ts:117-119`, inserted at `:158-160`).
  - Whether the `## Log` section already existed or was just added at the end of the file (`tasks.ts:253-271`).
  - The note's folder. Two notes with the same name look identical.
  - That the content was also copied to the clipboard. That copy happens silently and fails silently (`extractLog.ts:17-29`, `:72-75`).
  - It is plain text with no link to click.
- **Other notices:**
  - "No children" (`extractLog.ts:63`)
  - "No listItems metadata" (`extractLog.ts:57`)
  - "No wikilink found" (`extractLog.ts:109`)
  - A catch-all error shown for 8 seconds (`extractLog.ts:173-176`, `config.ts:20`)
- **Tests.** Nothing checks the success notice's text. The integration tests only check the "No children" and error notices (`tests/integration/extractLog.plugin.test.ts:43,362`). The test helper does record every notice (`tests/helpers/extractLogPluginTestHelper.ts:170-206`).
- **Similar command.** Complete project task's notice uses wikilink style: `Task completed and logged to [[Migration Initiative]].` (`tests/integration/completeProjectTask.plugin.test.ts:329-331`).

## Intended outcome (requirement)
After a successful Extract log, the notification tells the user where the content went, clearly enough that they don't need to open the target note to check.

## Questions that block progress
1. **What's missing from today's notice?** It already names the note and section. Which of these should be added?
   a. The dated sub-heading, e.g. `"Migration Initiative" > Log > [[2026-11-09 Mon]] Checkin mit Chris`
   b. The folder or full path, so same-named notes can be told apart
   c. A note when the Log section was just created
   d. That the content was copied to the clipboard
   e. A clickable link to the new spot
   f. Only rewording (for example, matching Complete project task's `[[Note]]` style)
   Also: could the user be on an older version that doesn't show this notice yet?
2. **If (e) is wanted:** a clickable notice adds UI behaviour and needs Obsidian code in `src/adapters/`. Is that in scope, or should the notice stay plain text?
3. **Should the notice stay visible longer than 4 seconds?** That's the shared success timeout, so changing it for every command is a separate decision.

## Assumptions (please confirm or correct)
- Only the wording or content of the success notice changes. Where content is inserted, the source link rewrite and the error notices stay the same.
- The notice is still shown only after both the target note and the source note have been updated.
- Users don't need a new setting for this.

## Acceptance cases (draft, to fill in once Q1 is answered)
- **Named link.** Extracting from `- Checkin mit Chris zu [[Migration Initiative]]` with children gives a notice naming `Migration Initiative`, the Log section, and whatever extra detail Q1 picks.
- **Bare link bullet.** For a bullet that's only a link (`- [[Project]]`), the notice reflects the heading built from the parent bullet.
- **Missing Log section.** If the target note has no Log section, the notice is accurate, and says the section was created if Q1(c) is chosen.
- **Custom heading.** With the log heading set to `### Inbox`, the notice says `Inbox`.
- **Unchanged cases.** No children → "No children" notice and no notice naming a destination. A failed write → error notice only.

## High-level plan
1. Write integration tests first that pin the exact success text in `tests/integration/extractLog.plugin.test.ts`, using the helper's `notice` field.
2. Move the message building into a pure helper in `src/utils/notices.ts`, next to `formatTransferNotice`, with unit tests. Its inputs would be the note name, section text, and the optional details chosen in Q1.
3. Call that helper from `extractLog.ts:168`. If the "section created" detail is wanted, `insertBlockAfterHeading` would need to report that back.
4. Add a CHANGELOG entry written from the user's point of view.

48.result:
# Requirements handoff: completing a task in a weekly, monthly or yearly note sends it to today's daily Log

## Intended outcome
When you tick a task `[x]` in a weekly, monthly or yearly note, the plugin should:
- mark the original line `[<]` (Scheduled), and
- put the task, completed `[x]`, under the Log heading of today's daily note (`dailyNoteLogHeading`, default `## Log`). It does not go under Todo.

The goal is that weekly, monthly and yearly notes never hold a completed task. The record of the work lives in the daily note. The `[<]` marker and the link back to the source note are the paper trail, which fits the "markdown file is the state" principle.

No owner replies yet (revision 1), so the questions below are still open.

## What happens today
- **Auto-move only runs in daily notes.** The tick-handling code skips any other kind of note (`src/events/autoMoveCompleted.ts:169`). A `[x]` ticked in a weekly, monthly or yearly note stays where it is.
- **Push task down works one level at a time.** Yearly goes to the current month, monthly to the current week, weekly to today (`src/utils/periodicNotes.ts:396-428`). It only runs when today falls inside the source period (`src/commands/pushTaskDown.ts:74`, `periodicNotes.ts:402`). It writes into the target's Todo section, merging with matching tasks there, and leaves terminal subtrees behind in the source (`pushTaskDown.ts:139-164`).
- **Project tasks are filed under a heading named after the note they were completed in** (`src/adapters/projectCompletion.ts:96-99`, `writeProjectCompletions`). The auto-move code already does this for `[[Project]]` tasks ticked in daily notes (`autoMoveCompleted.ts:203-228`).

## Firm requirements (from the request)
1. The trigger is completing a task (`[x]`) in a weekly, monthly or yearly note.
2. The original line becomes `[<]` (Scheduled). It is not deleted.
3. Today's daily note gets the task as `[x]` under `dailyNoteLogHeading`, not `periodicNoteTaskTargetHeading`.
4. The target is always **today's** daily note, even from monthly or yearly notes. There is no one-level-at-a-time step down.
5. Daily notes behave exactly as they do now.

## Open questions (these block implementation)
1. **Today outside the note's period.** What happens if you tick a task in last week's weekly note, or next month's monthly note? Options:
   - (a) send it to today's daily note anyway;
   - (b) leave it `[x]` in place and show a notice;
   - (c) something else.

   Push task down refuses in this case today.
2. **Ticked subtasks.** What about a task nested under an open parent, or a task under a `- [[Project]]` collector bullet? Options:
   - (a) only the ticked line moves; the parent stays open in the source;
   - (b) only top-level tasks qualify and nested ticks are left alone.

   The goal says "no completions in non-daily periodic notes", which points to (a).
3. **Project tasks (`[[Project]] …`).** Should they also be logged in the project note, the way daily-note ticks are? If so, which note should their sub-heading name: today's daily note (where the completion now lives) or the weekly, monthly or yearly source note?

## Assumptions (please correct any that are wrong)
- **A1.** It happens automatically when you tick, in the same tick-handler as daily-note auto-move. There is no new command. Ticking through the "Complete project task" command counts too.
- **A2.** It applies to a tick in any section of the note, not just Todo.
- **A3.** Started tasks (`[/]`) are left alone; only `[x]` triggers it.
- **A4.** Children travel the way they do with push task down: open children move with the task, and terminal subtrees stay in the source. Open children arrive in the daily Log unchanged.
- **A5.** If today's daily note doesn't exist, it is created (`getOrCreateFile`, `commandSetup.ts:71`). A missing Log heading is created, as `computeAutoMove` does now.
- **A6.** The task is inserted under Log without merging into the daily Todo, at the same position auto-move uses (`findLogInsertionLine`).
- **A7.** If writing to the daily note fails, the source is left exactly as it was.
- **A8.** Unticking afterwards does not reverse anything.
- **A9.** A source line that is already `[<]`, `[>]` or `[x]` and just gets edited does not trigger it. Only a change *to* `[x]` does (`detectAutoMoveCandidate`).

## Acceptance cases
| # | Given | When | Then |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Weekly note for this week, `- [ ] Call Sam` under Todo | tick it | weekly shows `- [<] Call Sam`; today's daily Log has `- [x] Call Sam` |
| 2 | Monthly note for this month | tick a task | it goes straight to today's daily Log, not to the weekly note |
| 3 | Yearly note for this year | tick a task | same as case 2 |
| 4 | Today's daily note doesn't exist | tick in the weekly note | daily note is created with Log and the `[x]` task |
| 5 | Task has an open child and a completed child | tick the parent | open child goes with it to the daily Log; completed child stays under the `[<]` line |
| 6 | Last week's weekly note | tick a task | **depends on Q1** |
| 7 | Nested subtask under an open parent in the weekly note | tick the subtask | **depends on Q2** |
| 8 | `[[Project]] Draft memo` in the weekly note | tick it | `[<]` in weekly, `[x]` in daily Log, plus a project log entry (**sub-heading depends on Q3**) |
| 9 | Started task `[/]` in the weekly note | mark it started | nothing happens (A3) |
| 10 | Daily note | tick a task in Todo | unchanged: it moves to Log as today |
| 11 | Writing to the daily note fails | tick in the weekly note | source line stays `[x]` and an error notice appears |

## Implementation plan (high level)
1. **Pure logic in `src/utils/`** (e.g. `autoMove.ts` or a sibling file): given the source text and the ticked line, work out the block to send (reusing `selectTransferableChildLines` or `getTransferableChildren`), the source edit (`markTaskAsScheduled` plus removing the transferred children), and the insertion into the daily Log (reusing `findLogInsertionLine` and the "create Log heading" branch). Write unit tests first.
2. **Changes in `autoMoveCompleted.ts`.** Replace the daily-only check at line 169 with routing: daily notes keep the current path, and weekly, monthly or yearly notes go to the new path. That path finds today's daily note with `formatPeriodPath(today, 'daily')` and `plugin.getToday`, uses `getOrCreateFile`, and writes with `vault.process`. Only after the write succeeds does it update the source, using the same "re-read the document, then confirm the line is unchanged" check the current code uses around its awaited writes. Project tasks reuse `completeProjectTaskAtLine` once Q3 is settled.
3. **Integration tests** for the cases above, using the patterns in `tests/CLAUDE.md`.
4. **Docs.** Add a CHANGELOG entry (e.g. "Completing a task in a weekly/monthly/yearly note files it in today's daily log"). Update the CLAUDE.md heading-settings table and the auto-move header comment.
